description: GitHub MCP Server Configuration (GitHub's official server; the archived @modelcontextprotocol/server-github is deprecated)

docker_alternative._comment: GitHub also ships the server as a Docker image for local or GitHub Enterprise use.

example_prompts: Search for repositories related to 'machine learning python'

get_file_contents.description: Read file contents from a repository
example_prompts: Get the contents of README.md from owner/repo
Show recent commits on the main branch
What changes were made in the last week?
Create an issue for the bug we found
Show open issues in the repository

pull_request_read.description: Get details of a specific PR
example_prompts: What changes are in the open PR?

token_setup.description: How to create a GitHub Personal Access Token
steps: 1. Go to GitHub Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens
2. Click 'Generate new token (classic)' or use fine-grained tokens
3. Select required scopes based on your needs
4. Copy the token and set it as the GITHUB_PAT environment variable

classic_token_scopes._comment: Classic scopes are coarse: public_repo already grants write access to public repositories, and there is no read-only classic scope for private ones. For read-only work, prefer a fine-grained token with read-only repository permissions.

use_fine_grained_tokens.description: Fine-grained tokens provide better security with limited scope

limit_repository_access.description: Only grant access to repositories Claude needs

code_review.description: Review PR changes and create issues for problems
prompts: Get the diff for PR #123 and review for security issues
Create an issue if any vulnerabilities are found
Read the README.md and compare with current code structure
Suggest documentation updates based on recent changes
Suggest appropriate labels based on issue content

permissions_example._comment: MCP tool permissions use the form mcp__<server>__<tool>. Tool names vary by server version; run /mcp in a session to list what the connected server actually exposes before pinning rules to names. As of November 7, 2026, GitHub's default tool set creates and updates issues with issue_write and reads pull requests with pull_request_read; create_issue appears only when the opt-in issues_granular feature flag is on, so the deny list names both. To rule out writes entirely, connect to https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly instead (or set GITHUB_READ_ONLY=1 for the Docker image).
